verdict: Recipe search sends user input straight to SQL. Bon appetit, attackers.
praise: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt at a sensible cost factor (snackstack/auth.py:18).

roasts.line: A live-looking Stripe key is committed in settings.py. It is not a secret if the whole internet has it.
roasts.fix: Rotate the key at the provider today, load it from STRIPE_KEY in the environment, add it to .env.example as a placeholder.

roasts.line: search() builds SQL with an f-string. Somewhere, a user named '; DROP TABLE recipes;-- is warming up.
roasts.fix: Use a parameterised query: cursor.execute("... WHERE title LIKE ?", (f"%{term}%",)).

roasts.line: DEBUG = True ships to production, so every crash hands visitors a free tour of the stack trace.
roasts.fix: Read DEBUG from the environment and default it to False.

verdict: One query per ingredient per recipe. The database has filed for overtime.
praise: Image thumbnails are generated once at upload and cached (snackstack/images.py:55).

roasts.line: The recipe list fetches ingredients one recipe at a time: 50 recipes, 51 queries, one tired database.
roasts.fix: Fetch ingredients for all listed recipes in one query (WHERE recipe_id IN (...)) and group in memory.

roasts.line: GET /recipes has no limit, so the homepage downloads the entire cookbook on every visit.
roasts.fix: Add limit and cursor parameters with a default page size of 20.

verdict: Lovely pitch, then step 3 sends me to a script that does not exist.
praise: The first paragraph says exactly who it is for and what it does (README.md:3).

roasts.line: Step 3 says `make seed`. The Makefile has never heard of seed. Day one, hour one.
roasts.fix: Add a seed target to the Makefile that runs scripts/seed.py, or change the README to the command that exists.

roasts.line: The app needs DATABASE_URL, but the only place that says so is a KeyError.
roasts.fix: Add .env.example listing DATABASE_URL and STRIPE_KEY, and fail with a message that names the missing variable.

verdict: utils.py is 1,212 lines. It is not a module, it is a lifestyle.
praise: Commit history is readable; the last 50 messages say what changed.

roasts.line: No CI at all. The test suite runs whenever someone remembers, which is never.
roasts.fix: Add .github/workflows/test.yml running pytest on pull requests.

roasts.line: `except Exception: pass` in the importer. Whatever went wrong, it has taken it to the grave.
roasts.fix: Catch the specific parse error, log the recipe id and the reason, and count failures in the import summary.

roasts.line: utils.py holds dates, money, slugs, emails and a hand-rolled CSV parser. Everything is a util if you believe hard enough.
roasts.fix: Split by topic into dates.py, money.py, text.py; replace the CSV parser with the csv module.

verdict: 'Something went wrong' is not an error message, it is a weather report.
praise: The API returns consistent JSON shapes with clear field names (snackstack/api/schemas.py:1).

roasts.line: The README promises 'export your cookbook as PDF'. The code promises nothing of the sort.
roasts.fix: Remove the claim until the export exists, or move it to a Roadmap section.

roasts.line: Every API failure returns {"error": "Something went wrong"}, including a typo in the recipe id.
roasts.fix: Return a specific message and code per case: 404 'recipe 812 not found', 422 with the invalid field.

verdict: FROM python:latest. A build that changes every week, like a mystery box.
praise: There is a CHANGELOG and it is actually up to date (CHANGELOG.md:1).

roasts.line: The Dockerfile pins nothing and runs as root, so every rebuild is a surprise with admin rights.
roasts.fix: Pin python:3.12-slim, add a non-root user, and add a .dockerignore.

roasts.line: The nutrition API call has no timeout. It will wait forever, which is longer than my shift.
roasts.fix: Pass timeout=5 to requests.get and return a cached value or a clear 503 when it expires.
